subject: Acme POC - access, success criteria, and evaluation plan
messages:
From: Emma Jones <emma.jones@acme.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, lukas_meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Acme POC - access, success criteria, and evaluation plan

Hi Marissa / Lukas,

Thanks again for today’s demo — really helpful. As discussed on the call, the Acme ML team is ready to move forward with a 2-week POC to validate latency, cost, and output quality on our customer support reranking workload.

Quick recap of what we need from Redwood to kick off the POC:
- A short written success criteria / evaluation plan we can sign off on (I attached our internal template).
- Temporary API credentials (test API key) + recommended rate limits for the POC.
- IP allowlist ranges for our staging environment (so we can open firewall rules).
- SSO invites for our two admins (david.patel@acme.com and it-admin@acme.com) so they can manage team access.

Target timeline: start week of Dec 7, evaluate through Dec 18, decision meeting the week of Dec 21. Does that work on your side?

Attached: Acme-POC-eval-plan-v1.docx (our template).

Thanks — Emma
Emma Jones
Head of ML Platform
Acme Corp

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Jones <emma.jones@acme.com>
Cc: lukas_meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 11:00:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Acme POC - access, success criteria, and evaluation plan

Hi Emma — great to hear and excited to run the POC with Acme.

Thanks for the clear list. I’ve taken a first pass at a proposed success criteria and evaluation plan (high level below) and attached our Redwood POC checklist and integration notes. If that looks good we’ll:
1) Provision a temporary API key and add the IP ranges you provide to our staging allowlist.
2) Send SSO invites (OIDC) to the admin emails you provided.
3) Share a lightweight dashboard so you can track latency, token usage, and quality metrics during the run.

Proposed success criteria (suggested, happy to iterate):
- Latency: 95th percentile inference latency <= 450ms for 512-token prompts on our dedicated POC pool.
- Cost: per-1000-token cost consistent with Redwood POC pricing (will provide estimate).
- Quality: reranking NDCG lift >= 12% vs baseline on provided eval set; no regression on precision@5.
- Stability: <1% error rate and no sustained outages >5 minutes.

Evaluation plan highlights:
- Week 0 (Dec 7): Provisioning, SSO invites, API key + smoke tests.
- Week 1 (Dec 8–14): Ingest sample traffic, run batch evals, tweak batching/quantization settings.
- Week 2 (Dec 15–18): Full-load runs with production-like traffic, collect metrics, prepare decision deck.

Owners:
- Redwood: marissa_cole (POC owner), lukas_meyer (SE / integration lead).
- Acme: Emma Jones (POC sponsor), David Patel (IT admin).

Can you confirm the IP ranges you want allowlisted and the preferred SSO admin emails? We’ll aim to have SSO invites and a temp key to you by end of day Thu (Dec 2).

Attachments: Redwood-POC-checklist.pdf (provisioning steps and dashboards).

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

From: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Jones <emma.jones@acme.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 14:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Acme POC - access, success criteria, and evaluation plan

Emma — quick tech notes from my side to make the engineering handoff smoother.

1) API & endpoints- POC endpoint: https://api.redwood.ai/v1/poc/acme/rerank- Auth: API Key (x-api-key header) for the temporary key we’ll issue.

2) Rate limits and quotas for POC- Default POC limit: 60 reqs/min, burstable to 150 reqs/min.
- If you need higher sustained throughput we can move you to the dedicated POC pool (let me know expected qps).

3) SSO / SAML / OIDC- We support OIDC-based SSO (preferred). For invites we need the admin email addresses as Marissa noted; you’ll receive an invite link and then we’ll accept your IDP metadata or test via Auth0/Okta.

4) IP allowlist- We need the CIDR ranges for your staging hosts. Common example: 203.0.113.0/24. If you prefer individual egress IPs provide those and we’ll add to the whitelist.

5) Sample curl (quick smoke test)
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/poc/acme/rerank" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "x-api-key: <TEMP_KEY>" -d '{"query":"sample","candidates":["a","b","c"]}'

Attached: network_requirements.pdf (firewall and TLS requirements).

I’ll stand by to provision the key once Marissa confirms the allowlist and we have the admin emails.

— Lukas
Lukas Meyer
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Emma Jones <emma.jones@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, lukas_meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 08:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Acme POC - access, success criteria, and evaluation plan

Thanks Marissa / Lukas — this all looks good. Confirming the details from our side:

IP allowlist (staging egress):
- 198.51.100.12/32
- 198.51.100.13/32

SSO admin invites please send to:
- david.patel@acme.com (IT Admin)
- it-admin@acme.com (Platform Admin)

We expect ~5 qps average during the POC with occasional spikes to 30 qps. If you think 60 reqs/min will be limiting, please bump to the dedicated POC pool.

Related links: I’ve uploaded our eval set and metrics baseline to the folder you shared: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-acme-poc

If you can provision the SSO invites and a temp API key by EOD Thu (Dec 2) that works for our engineers to do smoke tests on Fri.

Best — Emma

Subject: Re: Acme POC - access, success criteria, and evaluation plan

Perfect — thanks for the details, Emma.

We’ll do the following by EOD Thu (Dec 2):
- Add 198.51.100.12 and 198.51.100.13 to the POC allowlist.
- Issue SSO invites to david.patel@acme.com and it-admin@acme.com (OIDC flow).
- Provision a temporary API key with 500 reqs/day and rate limits set to 150 reqs/min (we can increase if you move to dedicated pool). Key: TEMP-ACME-DEC-02 (sent via separate secure channel).

Next steps (owners):
- marissa_cole: confirm when your team has accepted SSO invites and completed smoke test.
- lukas_meyer: monitor metrics and tweak batch/quant settings to meet latency target.
- Emma: run smoke tests and confirm baseline metrics in the shared Drive.

I’ll follow up with the secure key delivery and a quick runbook for smoke testing. Looking forward to getting started next week.

Thanks — Marissa
